inline_comments.comment: The early return for non-`@storybook/react-vite` frameworks is silent — no message is logged and no output is produced. A user running `storybook ai init` on, say, an Angular or Vue project will see nothing and have no idea why the command did nothing. At minimum, emit a `logger.warn` explaining the current limitation (e.g., 'This command currently only supports the @storybook/react-vite framework.') before returning, so the user is not left confused.

The JSON branch on line 53 correctly uses `console.log` for machine-consumable stdout piping, but the markdown branch here uses `console.log` where `logger.log` (imported at the top of the file) would be more consistent with the project convention that all non-machine diagnostic output flows through the canonical logger. Consider using `logger.log(generateMarkdownOutput(projectInfo))` for the markdown path.

`projectInfo.renderer || 'react'` should be `projectInfo.renderer ?? 'react'`. Per project conventions, `??` is preferred over `||` for default fallbacks. Since `renderer` is typed `string | null`, `||` would also replace an empty string `''` with `'react'`, silently masking a potentially misconfigured value, while `??` only replaces `null` or `undefined`.

The decorator example inside the generated code block uses JSX syntax (`<ThemeProvider>`, `<MemoryRouter>`, `<Story />`) but the file path comment above it says `preview.ts`, not `preview.tsx`. TypeScript does not allow JSX in `.ts` files — only `.tsx`. An AI agent or user following this example will get a compilation error (TS17004: 'Cannot use JSX unless the "--jsx" flag is provided' or 'This syntax requires an imported helper but module ... cannot be found'). Change the filename in the comment to `preview.tsx` in both the `hasCsfFactoryPreview` branch and the else branch.

`framework`, `renderer`, and `builder` are typed as `string | null`, but in `index.ts` they are always assigned via `data.frameworkPackage ?? 'unknown'`, meaning they can never actually be `null` at runtime. The type should be `string` (not `string | null`) so that consumers like `getPreviewConfigExample` don't need unnecessary null guards. The null-type is widening the interface beyond what the implementation actually produces.

The JSDoc comment says "Represents a skill category that can be expanded in the future." — this is stale terminology left over from when the command was called `skill`. Update to reflect the current naming (e.g., "Represents a structured AI prompt with a name, description, and detailed instructions.").

`import { aiInit } from '../ai';` is inserted between the `sandbox` and `upgrade` imports, but alphabetically `'../ai'` sorts before `'../doctor'`. Per the existing import ordering in this file, it should be placed before `import { doctor } from '../doctor'` around line 24.

`std-env` is not listed as a dependency in `code/lib/create-storybook/package.json`. The import works today only because of monorepo hoisting, but this is a fragile implicit dependency — it will break in stricter package managers, isolated installs, or if `std-env` is ever removed from a sibling package. Add `std-env` to the explicit `dependencies` (or `devDependencies`, if only used at build time) of `create-storybook`.

`logger.log('Detecting agent presence: ${detectAgent().name}')` runs unconditionally for every user, including non-agent runs. When no agent is detected, `detectAgent().name` is `undefined`, so every normal user sees `Detecting agent presence: undefined` in their terminal. This is noisy and exposes internal implementation details. Move this log inside the `if (isAgent)` block below, or change it to a debug-level log gated on agent detection.

`detectAgent()` is called three separate times: once at module load (for the `isAgent` constant), once on line 127 for the log, and again here for the log inside the `if (isAgent)` block. Since the result doesn't change between calls, capture it once at the top of the action callback: `const agent = detectAgent();` and reference `agent.name` in both log messages.

`await import('../../cli-storybook/src/ai')` is a deep relative path that crosses package boundaries directly into another monorepo package's `src/` directory, bypassing its public API surface. Per project conventions, cross-package imports should use the public package export (e.g., `import { aiInit } from '@storybook/cli-storybook/ai'`). Since `cli-storybook/package.json` currently only exports `./package.json`, a new entry in its `exports` map needs to be added (e.g., `"./ai": "./src/ai/index.ts"`), and then the import here should be updated accordingly.

general_comments.comment: No automated tests are included — all checkboxes in the PR checklist are unchecked. The new `aiInit` function, `getPrompts`/`generateMarkdownOutput`/`generateJsonOutput` helpers, `detectAgent` logic, and the framework-gate condition are entirely untested. At minimum, unit tests should cover: (1) `generateMarkdownOutput` and `generateJsonOutput` for a known `ProjectInfo` fixture; (2) `getDocsUrl` edge cases (`undefined` major version, a concrete version); (3) `detectAgent` returning the correct name for each environment-variable combination; and (4) the silent-return path for non-react-vite frameworks.

This PR introduces a second, parallel agent-detection implementation in `code/lib/create-storybook/src/bin/detect-agent.ts`, while an existing one already lives at `code/core/src/telemetry/detect-agent.ts`. The two files will diverge over time (e.g., if a new agent is added to one but not the other). Consider extracting the shared detection logic into a single utility in `code/core/src/telemetry/detect-agent.ts` (or a shared internal package) and re-exporting it, so there is one source of truth for which environment variables signal each agent.
